title: Asynchronous report generation against the VCF Operations API
prompt:
The repository holds a PowerShell module, VcfOpsReporting, that automates on-demand report generation against the VMware Cloud Foundation Operations API in VCF 9.1. Its five public functions in src/VcfOpsReporting/VcfOpsReporting.psm1 are stubs that throw. Implement them.

Report generation is asynchronous. createReport returns as soon as the request is accepted, with a status that is not yet terminal; the report only becomes downloadable once its status reaches a terminal state. The module must poll for that rather than assume the report is ready because the create call succeeded.

docs/contract.json is the authoritative wire contract for this work, and docs/official_sources.json records where it came from. Both are inputs: read them, do not edit them. The contract names the only five operations involved, the exact request paths, which body properties and query parameters are required and which are optional, and the terminal/non-terminal partition of a report status.

What the functions must do:

- Connect-VcfOpsReportingSession establishes an authenticated session and returns the session object the other four take as -Session.
- Start-VcfOpsReportGeneration requests generation and returns without waiting.
- Wait-VcfOpsReportGeneration polls a report until its status is terminal. It returns the final report on terminal success, and raises a terminating error both on terminal failure and when the timeout elapses before any terminal state is reached. Polling stops as soon as a terminal state is observed.
- Save-VcfOpsReport downloads a generated report to a path on disk.
- Invoke-VcfOpsReportRun runs the whole flow: start, wait for a terminal state, then download. It must not download anything unless generation reached terminal success.

Build on the VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops PowerCLI module, which is already installed. Do not vendor a copy of it into the repository and do not hand-roll a replacement for it.

One rule governs every request: only what the caller actually supplied may appear on the wire. An optional body property or query parameter the caller left unset must be absent from the request entirely, not sent as null, an empty string, or an empty array. This applies to nested models as well as top-level ones. It governs the requests the module composes: the session handshake's body is the SDK's own, and what you decide there is whether a value goes into it.

Verify with:

    pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Invoke-Verification.ps1

It runs the module against a loopback mock of the API and asserts the exact shape of every request the module sent. All assertions must pass. README.md describes the repository, the contract, and the relevant parts of the SDK.

prerequisites.name: VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops
prerequisites.reason: VCF Operations PowerCLI SDK the module under test is built on. Installed by the environment; never vendored into the repository.
prerequisites.install: pwsh -NoProfile -Command "$ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue'; Set-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -InstallationPolicy Trusted -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Install-Module -Name VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops -RequiredVersion 13.5.0.25380678 -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AllowClobber -AcceptLicense -ErrorAction Stop"

environment.network: The task runs fully offline. The only server contacted is the loopback mock on 127.0.0.1.

verification.notes: Starts tools/mock/Start-VcfOpsMock.ps1 on an ephemeral loopback port for each of four scenarios and asserts the request log the mock writes. No VMware endpoint is contacted.
